slot.brief: Given a change in T and P for the same gas (or a comparison of two gases), find the new density or the ratio of densities using ρ = PM/RT; medium algebra but no unit traps.

stem: An ideal gas has a density of $1.80\ \text{g L}^{-1}$ at pressure $P$ and temperature $T$. At constant pressure, increasing the temperature by $100\ \text{K}$ reduces the density to $1.35\ \text{g L}^{-1}$. The density of this gas at a pressure of $2.4P$ and temperature of $(T - 60\ \text{K})$ is:
working:
According to the ideal gas equation:
$$\rho = \dfrac{PM}{RT} \implies \rho \propto \dfrac{P}{T}$$

**Step 1: Find the initial temperature $T$**
At constant pressure ($P_1 = P_2 = P$):
$$\dfrac{\rho_2}{\rho_1} = \dfrac{T_1}{T_2}$$
Given $\rho_1 = 1.80\ \text{g L}^{-1}$, $\rho_2 = 1.35\ \text{g L}^{-1}$, $T_1 = T$, and $T_2 = T + 100\ \text{K}$:
$$\dfrac{1.35}{1.80} = \dfrac{T}{T + 100}$$
$$\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{T}{T + 100} \implies 4T = 3T + 300 \implies T = 300\ \text{K}$$

**Step 2: Identify conditions at State 3**
$$P_3 = 2.4P$$
$$T_3 = T - 60\ \text{K} = 300\ \text{K} - 60\ \text{K} = 240\ \text{K}$$

**Step 3: Calculate the new density $\rho_3$**
$$\dfrac{\rho_3}{\rho_1} = \left(\dfrac{P_3}{P_1}\right)\left(\dfrac{T_1}{T_3}\right)$$
$$\rho_3 = 1.80 \times \left(\dfrac{2.4P}{P}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{300\ \text{K}}{240\ \text{K}}\right)$$
$$\rho_3 = 1.80 \times 2.4 \times 1.25 = 1.80 \times 3.0 = 5.40\ \text{g L}^{-1}$$

(Alternatively, referencing State 2: $\rho_3 = 1.35 \times 2.4 \times \dfrac{400}{240} = 1.35 \times 4.0 = 5.40\ \text{g L}^{-1}$)

Independent check: At constant P, ρ ∝ 1/T: 1.80·T = 1.35·(T+100) → T = 300 K. Since ρ ∝ P/T, ρ' = 1.80 × (2.4P/P) × (300/240) = 1.80 × 2.4 × 1.25 = 5.40 g/L.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A ($3.60\ \text{g L}^{-1}$) comes from a sign error in temperature: taking $T_3 = T + 60\ \text{K} = 360\ \text{K}$ instead of $T - 60\ \text{K} = 240\ \text{K}$, giving $\rho_3 = 1.80 \times 2.4 \times (300/360) = 3.60\ \text{g L}^{-1}$.
Option B ($4.05\ \text{g L}^{-1}$) comes from applying the State 1-to-3 multiplier ($3.0$) to the intermediate density $\rho_2 = 1.35\ \text{g L}^{-1}$ instead of $\rho_1 = 1.80\ \text{g L}^{-1}$, giving $1.35 \times 3.0 = 4.05\ \text{g L}^{-1}$.
Option D ($7.20\ \text{g L}^{-1}$) comes from cross-state confusion: using initial density $\rho_1 = 1.80\ \text{g L}^{-1}$ but taking $T_2 = 400\ \text{K}$ as the initial temperature in the ratio, giving $1.80 \times 2.4 \times (400/240) = 7.20\ \text{g L}^{-1}$.
